evidence.V1: Reads instantly as a cut gem from every view: front outline is a clean symmetric crown-over-point diamond, three-quarter silhouette keeps the faceted crown and sharp culet, top shows a crisp octagonal table; A15 X/Y error 0.0.
evidence.V2: Big crown/pavilion split and medium table + 8 crown facets + girdle band read, but there is no small tier (no star/kite facets, no table bevel or sparkle detail), so hierarchy stops at two levels.
evidence.V3: Plain octagonal frustum on an octagonal cone; crown is about as tall as the pavilion and nothing is pushed or exaggerated, so it reads as a correct but stiff primitive gem rather than a confident stylised one.
evidence.V4: Girdle band is the only light-catching break; every facet edge is a razor hard edge with no ~0.045 chamfer, unlike the bevelled rims on the kit anchors, so edge treatment is inconsistent.
evidence.V5: Close-ups (crown/pavilion, studio and flat) show flat planar facets with no pinches, seams, z-fighting or overlap; A18 pass, 0 flipped faces, 0 cap overlaps.
evidence.V6: One hue in three values (light table, mid crown, dark pavilion), carried cleanly through teal, royal and crimson colourways; disciplined.
evidence.V7: 64 tris against the tiny-class target of 150 (ceiling 300).
evidence.V8: One white LF_VertexColor material and one-hue-in-3-values match the kit, but no chamfers and fully faceted shading versus the kit's chamfered, smooth-shaded look make it a minor mismatch beside the anchors.
evidence.V9: Studio line is correct for a pickup: CanCollide off, CanTouch on, Box fidelity, Anchored, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin centre.

top_fixes: Add the kit chamfer (~0.045 studs) on the girdle and table edges so the facets catch a highlight line like the anchors' bevelled rims
Add a small-detail tier: a narrow bevel ring around the table and/or star facets on the crown so the gem has big/medium/small hierarchy
Push the stylisation: lower the crown and deepen the pavilion (or widen the table) so the proportion reads as a deliberate stylised gem rather than a frustum on a cone
Consider a subtle top-light value step on the table (lightest value) vs crown facets to sharpen read at 64 px
